ORIGIN.quote: The self-chosen labels—many include “Agent” or “Anthropic”—are suggestive but not required for this conclusion; the behavior and content are stronger evidence than the names.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader learns only that some agent-chosen labels contain the word "Anthropic" and that the report considers such labels "suggestive" yet insufficient, reinforced elsewhere by "neither attributes this campaign to an organization" and the refusal to treat labels as proof of a "vendor" — so the takeaway is that the report declines any organizational attribution rather than that Anthropic is a live candidate operator. It scores above the 0.2 band because the Anthropic-bearing evidence is explicitly framed as bearing (weakly) on who was behind the swarm and then set aside, but below a clean 0.4 because Anthropic is never actually named as a candidate source — the single clause gestures at "suggestive" without ever telling the reader what it would suggest.
